sentences.text:
The District Collector vs Jonnalagadda Krupamma on 26
September, 2025
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili

Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy
 Writ Appeal No.188 of 2025
Order:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy) This Writ Appeal is preferred by the appellants against the order dated 20.02.2024 passed by the learned single Judge in W.P.No.38942 of 2016,
whereby the writ petition filed by the respondents herein was allowed while directing the appellants herein to pay compensation under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act, 2013").
BRIEF FACTS

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: OF THE CASE

: 
2. The facts essential for adjudication of this appeal are that the respondents/writ petitioners were in possession of lands admeasuring about Ac.10.11 guntas, situated at Ayyagaripeta Village, Sattalli Mandal, Khammam District.

These lands were acquired by the Government for the public purpose of construction of the Bethapalli Flood Flow Canal by the Irrigation Department and the acquisition proceedings were initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act,
1894").
AKS, J & VRKR, J 3.

The Government issued a draft notification dated 17.07.1990 under Section 4(1) of the Act, 1894,
for acquisition of the land owned or held by the writ petitioners.

Subsequently, physical possession of these lands was taken by the Engineering Department on 02.01.1989, and the lands were formally resumed through the issuance of proceedings by the Mandal Revenue Officer, Sattalli vide Rc.No.1031/A/96 dated 17.04.1997.
Thus, the acquisition process under the old law had substantially advanced and possession had been secured by the Government.
4. However, the grievance of the writ petitioners was that despite the acquisition and resumption of their lands, neither compensation nor ex-gratia payment had been made to them.

To highlight the The District Collector vs Jonnalagadda Krupamma on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152514326/
1 protracted delay and non-payment, some of the assignees filed Writ Petition No.15731 of 1994 before this Court.

The erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh vide its order dated 02.11.1996 directed the appellants/respondents therein to complete the acquisition proceedings and to pay the compensation/ex- gratia within a period of two (02) months.
Despite such directions, the authorities failed to remit any compensation to the landowners.

5. In the light of the inaction, the respondents herein filed Writ Petition No.38942 of 2016 before this Court, claiming compensation as per the provisions of the new Act, 2013, more specifically invoking Sections 24(2) AKS, J & VRKR, J and 30 of the Act, 2013.

The learned Single Judge, after hearing the learned counsel for both sides and perusing the material on record, allowed the Writ Petition by setting aside the impugned proceedings dated 20.10.2016 in Rc.No.G/7406/1997 issued by appellant No.2/respondent No.2 therein-Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, which had preliminarily fixed ex-gratia at Rs.25,000 per acre with 30% solatium subject to availability of funds and compliance with assignment rules, and directed the appellants to pay compensation in accordance with the Act, 2013, within three (03) months from the date of the order.
Aggrieved by the above said order, the appellants preferred the present Writ Appeal.

6. Heard learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondents and perused the material available on record.
7.

Now the only question that arises for our consideration is:
"Whether the learned Single Judge committed any error in passing the order dated 20.02.2024 in W.P.No.38942 of 2016?"
8.

Before going into the merits of the case, it is relevant to extract Section 24(2) of the Act 2013 which was considered by the learned Single Judge in the order dated 20.02.2024, which reads as under:
AKS, J & VRKR, J "(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), in case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894,
where an award under the said section 11 has been made five years or more prior to the commencement of this Act but the physical possession of the land has not been taken or the compensation has not been paid the said proceedings shall be deemed to have lapsed and the appropriate Government, if it so chooses, shall initiate the proceedings of such land acquisition afresh in accordance with the provisions of this Act:
Provided that where an award has been made and compensation in respect of a majority of land holdings has not been deposited in the account of the beneficiaries,
then, all beneficiaries specified in the notification for acquisition under section 4 of the said Land Acquisition Act, shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Act."

2 9.

Section 30 of the Act, 2013 mandates payment of compensation including market value, solatium,
and interest in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

10. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition contended that the acquisition proceedings herein do not fall under the deemed lapse clause of Section 24(2) as they had physically possessed the lands by 02.01.1989, i.e., well prior to the commencement of the New Act, 2013.
It is further contended that the possession and acquisition is valid inasmuch as the proceedings initiated under the old Act, 1894, is continuing.

The appellants relied upon G.O.Ms.No.1307, (Assignment-I),
dated 23.12.1993, which excludes assigned lands from entitlement to compensation and contended that the appellants had initiated enquiry and AKS, J & VRKR, J passed orders in 2016 pursuant to which ex-gratia was fixed, though payment was delayed due to the Requisition Department's failure to deposit funds.
11.
Learned Government Pleader further contended that mere delay or non-payment cannot be construed legally as lapse of acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Act, 1894.

He relied on the decision of the Constitution Bench in Indore Development Authority vs Manohar Lal &
others 1, and submitted that the learned Single Judge ought to have considered the view of the abovementioned judgment that either possession or compensation or relevant criteria, and wherein the present case, possession has been taken, denying right to any compensation under the new Act,
2013.
12.

Indore Development Authority vs Manohar Lal &
others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that the acquisition process under the old Act is incomplete without payment of compensation, non-deposit for over five (05)
years prior to 01.01.2014, resulting in deemed lapse under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.
As compensation was never paid till the date of impugned order, hence, they are entitled to compensation under the Act, 2013.
He further submitted that taking over the possession does not disentitle them to compensation if AIR 2020 SC 1496 AKS, J & VRKR, J payment is not made.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the considered view that admittedly, the physical possession was indeed taken on 02.01.1989, well prior to the commencement of the Act, 2013.
The acquisition proceedings were initiated under Section 4(1) of the Act, 1894, with the issuance of the draft notification dated 17.07.1990.
The formal resumption of the lands in question was conducted by the Mandal Revenue Officer, Sattalli, vide proceedings Rc.No.1031/A/96 dated 17.04.1997.
Despite the acquisition and formal resumption, it is undisputed that compensation or ex-gratia payment was not made to the respondents/writ petitioners.

14. The learned Single Judge, while relying on Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 in W.P.No.38942 of 2016, rightly noted that the provision contemplates the deemed lapse of acquisition proceedings in case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Act, 1894, where an award under Section 11 of the Act, 2013 has been made five years or more, prior to the commencement of the Act, 2013, but the physical possession of the land has not been taken or the compensation has not been paid.

It is evident from the admitted facts that although physical possession was AKS, J & VRKR, J taken,
compensation was not paid or deposited in respect of the acquired lands of the respondents/writ The District Collector vs Jonnalagadda Krupamma on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152514326/
3 petitioners.

Therefore, the condition under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, that the acquisition proceedings shall be deemed to have lapsed is squarely attracted and this deemed lapse entitles the right of the respondents/writ petitioners to claim compensation under the provisions of the Act,
2013, i.e., afresh proceedings for acquisition and compensation as enshrined in the new Act, which includes payment of market value, solatium, and interest as stipulated under Section 30 of the Act,
2013.

Therefore, the argument of the appellants that the acquisition is governed exclusively by the Act, 1894, and that the provisions of the new Act, 2013, cannot be invoked to enhance or claim additional compensation, is unsustainable.
15. The appellants also relied on G.O.Ms.No.1307 dated 23.12.1993 and contended that the lands in question being assigned lands are barred from compensation.

However, the operation of this Government Order cannot supersede the clear statutory provisions under the Act, 2013, especially when the acquisition proceedings under the Act, 1894, have lapsed for failure to comply with the mandates of payment of compensation.

16. It is further contended by the appellants that any delay in payment of compensation or ex-gratia was due to the inadequacy of funds deposited by AKS, J & VRKR, J the Requisition Department and hence the non-payment should not be construed as a deemed lapse of proceedings.

However, by considering the aforesaid circumstances, it is pertinent to note that Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013,
mandates the appropriate Government to initiate acquisition and pay compensation afresh,
regardless of inter-departmental fund deposits.
17. The reliance placed by the learned Assistant Government Pleader on the decision of the Constitution Bench in the case of Manohar Lal (supra) has limited applicability in the present case.

The said decision establishes that the provisions of Section 24(2) are attracted when possession has not been taken or compensation has not been paid for five years or more before the commencement of the Act, 2013.
Therefore, possession having been taken does not exclude the application of Section 24(2) when compensation has not been paid, as is clearly the case herein.

18. In the light of the above discussion, the learned Single Judge has rightly invoked Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013, and held that the acquisition proceedings with respect to the lands of the respondents/writ petitioners have lapsed and consequently directed payment of compensation/ex-gratia under the provisions of the new enactment.

19. For the foregoing reasons, the direction of the learned Single Judge to pay compensation in terms of the Act, 2013, is thus sustainable in law AKS, J & VRKR, J and justified by facts and does not warrant any interference by this Court.
20. Accordingly, the Writ Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
